description: Pre-registered A1-A8 ablation study designs and decision rules for Open-XTTS-Trainer (REMEDIATION_PLAN.md §11.5, §12.3.C Item 7). Fixed in advance before experimental execution to enforce research integrity and eliminate p-hacking.

calibration.empirical_basis: Run 5 Modal A100 baseline across 5 eval languages (en, es, fr, de, hi), 900 utterances, 3 random seeds
calibration.zero_leakage_policy: Speaker similarity evaluated using independent ECAPA2 (arXiv:2401.08395), never XTTS's internal H/ASP conditioning encoder (avoiding encoder leakage; arXiv:2506.20190).

global_guardrails.why: General intelligibility on held-out evaluation voices must not regress beyond the 95% CI noise floor.
Character-level error rate must not regress.
Speaker similarity across unseen held-out voices must not regress (catastrophic forgetting check).
Predicted naturalness relative to paired baseline must not regress beyond the subjective noise floor.
Candidate must produce zero additional empty audio, babbling loops (>2.2x duration & >=1.0s excess), or NaNs.

A1.title: Short-Text Hallucination Mitigation
A1.question: What training recipe change eliminates short-text hallucinations in autoregressive speech modeling?
A1.decision_rule: Compare all 12 grid configurations against baseline. A cell is eligible if its short-prompt CER 95% CI upper bound is <= baseline long-prompt CER 95% CI upper bound (category 'long_complex', CER margin <= 0.01) and held-out speaker similarity does not regress (SECS worst CI improvement >= -0.02). Among eligible cells, adopt the most computationally efficient configuration, defined as the minimum short_clip_mix_ratio (primary) and fewest total training steps to reach the validation loss plateau (secondary; GPU-hours tiebreaker).

gates.why: Short-prompt CER must remain within the pre-registered 95% CI noise floor (margin 0.01) without hallucination regressions.
Candidate must produce zero additional duration or audio failures on short prompts.

A2.title: DVAE Fine-Tuning Utility Across Domains
A2.question: Does fine-tuning Stage 1 DVAE yield downstream synthesis gains compared to the stock DVAE or an encoder-frozen variant?
A2.decision_rule: Documented architectural exception to the default frozen-DVAE invariant (README.md Stage 1 Invariant): Retraining or fine-tuning the Stage 1 DVAE alters discrete codebook token assignments and invalidates pretrained Stage 2 GPT checkpoints, requiring a mandatory Stage 2 GPT retrain from scratch. Recommend Stage 1 DVAE fine-tuning only for acoustic-shifted domains where downstream Stage 2 end-to-end intelligibility (WER lower 95% CI improvement > 0.0) or SECS (lower 95% CI improvement > 0.0) demonstrates statistically significant gains over stock DVAE that justify the full Stage 2 retraining compute cost.

gates.why: End-to-end intelligibility must not regress beyond the noise floor under Stage 1 DVAE adaptation.
End-to-end speaker similarity must not regress beyond the noise floor under Stage 1 DVAE adaptation.

citations: Zheng et al. (Online Clustered Codebook, ICCV 2023)

A3.title: Conditioning Masking Impact (F2 Bug Verification)
A3.question: What is the empirical effect of upstream batch conditioning masking vs. per-sample conditioning masking on speech stability?

setup.evaluation: Paired N=300 per seed, across 3 seeds on base eval voices.

A3.decision_rule: Retain per-sample masking fix (mandatory correctness); report measured effect sizes on duration ratio stability and short-prompt CER in paper table.

gates.why: Per-sample conditioning masking must not regress short-prompt character error rate beyond the noise floor.
Per-sample conditioning masking must preserve speaker similarity within the 95% CI noise floor margin.

A4.title: Prompt Conditioning: Same-Clip vs. Cross-Clip Reference
A4.question: Does training with same-clip masked prompts leak acoustic shortcuts compared to pairing with different clips from the same speaker?
A4.decision_rule: Adopt cross-clip prompting as default if SECS on held-out evaluation clips improves beyond the noise floor (worst CI improvement > +0.02) without regressing intelligibility (CER CI <= +0.01).

gates.why: Cross-clip prompt conditioning must improve speaker similarity beyond the 0.02 noise floor margin.
Cross-clip prompting must not regress character error rate beyond the 0.01 margin.

A5.title: Text Representation for Unseen Scripts
A5.question: What text representation strategy best transfers XTTS to a new script: BPE vocabulary expansion, per-character tokens, or phonetic romanization?
A5.decision_rule: Select the representation with the lowest target CER that preserves base language tokenization identity (test_extended_tokenizer_preserves_base passes and base CER CI degradation <= +0.01).

gates.why: Base language CER must be preserved within the 0.01 noise floor margin when extending text representation.

A6.title: Punctuation and Alignment Pause Consistency
A6.question: Does enforcing punctuation-to-acoustic pause consistency via forced alignment reduce pacing and prosodic errors?
A6.decision_rule: Make alignment pause-consistency validator blocking if candidate achieves statistically significant gain in UTMOS (worst 95% CI improvement > +0.10) while maintaining zero duration_ratio failure regressions (failures difference <= 0, eval/harness.py duration_ratio failure count).

gates.why: Alignment pause-consistency must achieve statistically significant naturalness improvement (worst 95% CI improvement > +0.10).
Candidate must produce zero duration_ratio failure regressions under alignment pause validation.

A7.title: Multilingual Replay Ratio for New Language Adaptation
A7.question: What proportion of base-language replay data prevents catastrophic forgetting when adapting to a new language?
A7.decision_rule: Select the minimum replay ratio where base-language WER and SECS degradation remains within noise margins (WER degradation <= 0.02, SECS degradation <= 0.02) while minimizing training step overhead on target CER.

gates.why: Base-language WER must not degrade beyond the 0.02 noise floor margin under multilingual replay.
Base-language speaker similarity SECS must not degrade beyond the 0.02 margin under multilingual replay.

citations: Yang et al. (Lifelong Multilingual TTS, 2021, arXiv:2110.04482)

A8.title: Stage 3 HiFi-GAN Fine-Tuning Utility
A8.question: Does fine-tuning the HiFi-GAN vocoder on teacher-forced GPT latents provide perceptible quality improvements over the stock vocoder?
A8.decision_rule: Retain Stage 3 vocoder fine-tuning only if the tuned decoder achieves a statistically significant improvement in predicted naturalness (UTMOS lower 95% CI > 0.0) without regressing speaker similarity (SECS CI >= -0.02).

gates.why: Tuned Stage 3 HiFi-GAN decoder must achieve statistically significant naturalness improvement (UTMOS lower 95% CI > 0.0).
Speaker similarity SECS must not regress beyond the 0.02 noise floor margin under vocoder fine-tuning.
